candidate.title: DP-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle row labelled DP-Seq in the supplied Illumina crop: design of a defined heptamer primer set, Poly(A) selection, first-strand cDNA synthesis, primer hybridization and PCR to DNA. DP-seq is the spelling used in the matched primary paper, not a separate method. The neighboring Quartz-seq2 and Smart-Seq/NanoCAGE rows are separate catalogue entries, not alternatives of this assigned DP-Seq schematic. The cited mouse-transcriptome implementation clarifies primer chemistry and the boundary between the depicted amplicons and subsequent sequencing-library preparation; its unshown experiments, primer-set variants and adaptor routes are not additional extracted workflows.

operations.label: Define set of heptamer primers
operations.description: Select primer-binding sites less likely to form local secondary structure and positioned to yield identifiable transcript sequence; produce a defined primer set specification. The left hairpins explain selection criteria rather than conversion of structured RNA into unstructured RNA.
operations.mechanism: Reference-guided selection of heptamer targeting sequences. The matched paper incorporates predicted single-stranded cDNA accessibility and sequence uniqueness; this is a design operation.
operations.information_effect: The design output specifies the physical reagent s_primers; the graph uses a precedence link to its application because no primer-manufacture operation is drawn. It restricts which transcript regions can be efficiently represented and favors regions informative for transcript assignment without guaranteeing unique mapping of every read.

operations.mechanism: Targeting heptamer segments hybridize to cDNA; the universal tails become amplifiable terminal sequence through the following extension/amplification block.

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Extend the annealed primers and amplify the resulting cDNA-derived fragments to produce multiple DNA copies. The single broad PCR block is retained; the matched paper resolves the initial-extension chemistry within it.
operations.mechanism: In the matched DP-seq implementation, Klenow polymerase first extends partially hybridized primers; Taq polymerase then forms and amplifies double-stranded products whose ends include the full tailed-primer sequences. This is more specific than ordinary PCR directly from untailored seven-base primers.
operations.information_effect: Produces a DNA amplicon library of selected regions of poly(A)-selected transcripts. The paper reports relative transcript-abundance measurements from subsequently prepared sequencing libraries, with biases from cDNA structure, fragment length, GC content and incomplete reverse transcription. Sequencing can support transcript identity and relative expression for represented regions; unique transcript assignment is conditional on sequence uniqueness. No cell barcode or UMI is depicted in this DP-Seq row.

Paper-derived chemistry is limited to the matched Bhargava implementation and explains the broad schematic blocks.
